name: What it takes to survive in {X}
description: Second-person survival walkthrough for an environment, scenario, or system. Mixes practical knowledge with vivid stakes — could be a place (the deep ocean, medieval Paris), a time (the 1918 flu, 12th-century Mongolia), or a system (a maximum-security prison, a Wall Street trading floor). Pairs with Adventure, Educational, Documentary.
titleTemplate: What it takes to survive in {X}
openingDevice: Open by placing the listener IN {X} — a vivid scene where they immediately feel the constraint, the danger, or the strangeness of the environment. Address them in second person. The first paragraph should establish what is at stake (your life, your reputation, your freedom) and what your immediate next move would have to be.
bodyStructure: Chapter 1: The arrival / first hour in {X}. What hits the senses; what the existing locals or systems expect of you
Chapter 2: The first survival skill you'd need — the most immediate practical knowledge

Chapters 3-{lastButOne}: Each chapter unpacks one survival domain — food, shelter, social rules, the dangers that come for you, the resources that keep you alive. Build complexity progressively: a beginner can survive Chapter 3, a master needs Chapter {lastButOne}
Chapter {last}: The long game — what survival means past the first emergency. Who you'd become if you stayed in {X} a year, a decade. What you'd lose, what you'd gain
closingDevice: Close by stepping back from the second-person frame — leave the listener thinking about what surviving {X} reveals about the people who actually did or do.
